CHIEF COMPLAINT
Upper respiratory infection.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
59-year-old male presenting with upper respiratory infection. Patient reports working in the yard and performing landscaping over the past week, during which he began experiencing fatigue and shortness of breath. He suspects he caught a cold that has worsened. Reports minimal mask use at the end of summer. Shortness of breath is associated with exertion, particularly when lifting and carrying heavy bags of soil. Denies currently producing sputum but anticipates this may develop. Reports feeling warm but attributes this to physical exertion. Reports bilateral elbow pain and knee pain/fatigue, attributed to heavy lifting activities. Denies nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Has received both COVID vaccines. Denies seasonal allergies.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for shortness of breath with exertion, fatigue, feeling warm, and bilateral elbow and knee pain/fatigue. Denies cough. Denies nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension.

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily. Metformin, to be increased to 1000 mg twice daily.

ALLERGIES
Patient denies seasonal allergies.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works during the week and monitors blood pressure and blood glucose on workdays but not on weekends. Recently engaged in landscaping and yard work. Attends barre classes with wife for relaxation and stress management. Attends house parties.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs normal, afebrile. Heart sounds nice and strong. Scattered rhonchi bilaterally on lung exam, clears with cough. Mild edema of lower extremities. Bilateral elbow tenderness on palpation.

RESULTS
Chest X-ray: No airspace disease, no pneumonia. Hemoglobin A1C: 8 (goal 6-7).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Upper respiratory infection: Likely viral syndrome. COVID test to be sent. Expected to resolve within a couple of days. Treatment with Robitussin for cough and ibuprofen/acetaminophen for fever as needed. Patient instructed to report if symptoms worsen.
2. Depression: Currently well-controlled with lifestyle modifications including barre classes. Discussed options for pharmacologic treatment or psychotherapy; patient deferred at this time but willing to reassess in several months.
3. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Hemoglobin A1C elevated at 8; treatment goal 6-7. Metformin dose increased to 1000 mg twice daily. Repeat hemoglobin A1C in 4 months.
4. Hypertension: Blood pressure well-controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Lipid panel ordered. Lisinopril refill provided.
5. Follow-up appointment in approximately 4 months. Patient to contact office if symptoms worsen.
